# Neurochemical Recipe Book

*Written 2026-11-22. Generated by `neuro_recipes.py` (data, tests in `tests/test_neuro_recipes.py`). Sources are in `references/NeuroRecipes/` and `ContextPlease/claude/references/INDEX.md`.*

A recipe is the mix the Tone character carries: seven levels, one per chemical, in kite order and rainbow order. Level 0 is black, level 1 is white, and the pure hue sits at the baseline: brighter is warmer, darker is more negative. The seven together are the Emotional Spectrum of a word, and the same seven describe the user (read from the input) and Ptolemy (set by the dispenser).

**How the numbers were set.** The papers give the direction of each chemical on each state (arouses, inhibits, raised, lowered), not a magnitude. Every level is a five-step engineering setpoint (.1 .3 .5 .7 .9, with .05/.15/.95 at the extremes) chosen from those directions. Each recipe lists the sources that fix its directions and the test that moves its numbers; a test result sets the next revision.

## 1. The seven

| position | colour | chemical | silk (orbweaver name) | what it does to word choice and sentence build | emotion-linked sentences / papers in the 40-paper corpus |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| hub | red | OPI | SHELL | comfort, safety, "liking"; inhibits RAGE and GRIEF; the protective container: the reply is held, not pushed (`echo_cap`, `relax_rate`) | 126 / 13 |
| axis 1 | orange | GLU | SPAN | excitatory drive: how far the reply reaches and how much it carries (`pool_size`, `hops`) | 71 / 17 |
| axis 1 | yellow | GABA | WRAP | brake and noise filter: encloses the reply, prunes loops and heat (`prune_floor`, `echo_cap`) | 154 / 21 |
| axis 2 | green | DA | HOOK | SEEKING: curiosity and novelty; catches interest, marks progress (`novelty_rank`) | 192 / 27 |
| axis 2 | blue | 5HT | ELABORATE | patience, coping, inhibition; stretches a reply over several steps without breaking (`coherence`) | 331 / 23 |
| axis 3 | indigo | NE | SCAFFOLD | gain on attention and urgency; temporary structure that narrows the frame (`short_frame`) | 55 / 20 |
| axis 3 | violet | OXT | ANCHOR | social alignment: anchors the reply to the user and their words (`user_boost`); also raises in-group bias, so it is paired with NE | 66 / 14 |

The silk names are the orbweaver slot names (`ANCHOR SPAN SCAFFOLD ELABORATE HOOK WRAP SHELL`). The chemical sets the knob; the silk says which job that knob does in the reply. The pairs on one axis oppose each other in the sources: GLU against GABA (excite against inhibit), DA against 5HT (approach and impulse against patience and restraint), NE against OXT (alarm against social safety: CRH drives the locus coeruleus, oxytocin and opioids quiet GRIEF). The hub, OPI, is the recovery chemistry.

**Why OPI and not CB1.** The Gemini hub was CB1. Across the 40 papers CB1 has 23 emotion-linked sentences in 7 papers; the opioid system has 126 in 13, and Panksepp names opioids as inhibitors of both RAGE and GRIEF. CB1 stays on the reserve list below and is retested if the fit asks for it.

Baseline (the pure hue): OPI 0.50, GLU 0.45, GABA 0.65, DA 0.50, 5HT 0.75, NE 0.30, OXT 0.50.

## 2. Recipes

Columns: OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT (kite order).

### Primary systems (Panksepp)

**SEEKING**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.50 | 0.70 | 0.50 | 0.90 | 0.60 | 0.55 | 0.50 |

- Fixed by: PANK: DA drives the medial-forebrain-bundle system: curiosity, anticipatory eagerness, planning; DID: DA is the substrate of intrinsic motivation: interest, positive affect, cognitive flexibility
- Language: long runs, questions, associative leaps, "what if"
- Use: user is exploring; Ptolemy follows with candidates one step beyond the prompt
- Test: novelty_rank of picks rises with DA; reply length tracks

**RAGE**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.10 | 0.90 | 0.10 | 0.70 | 0.10 | 0.90 | 0.20 |

- Fixed by: PANK: substance P and GLU arouse RAGE; opioids and GABA inhibit it; thwarted SEEKING provokes it; CH: reduced 5HT raises impulsive and aggressive behaviour; QUI: OXT can enhance anti-social behaviour (envy, gloating, aggression); GEM: rage row: DA .90 5HT .05 NE .95 GLU .90
- Language: clipped imperatives, repetition, absolutes, profanity
- Use: user state to cancel; also the source of the gated WRATH recipe
- Test: user-side detector separates RAGE from FEAR on DA direction

**FEAR**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.30 | 0.80 | 0.10 | 0.30 | 0.30 | 0.90 | 0.20 |

- Fixed by: PANK: CRF and NPY regulate FEAR; benzodiazepines inhibit it through GABA; NUSS: GABA agonists in the amygdala reduce fear, antagonists are anxiogenic; GOD: CRH drives locus coeruleus firing, which releases NE forebrain-wide
- Language: hedging, interrogatives, catastrophising, fear-domain nouns
- Use: user state to cancel
- Test: detector: NE high with DA low

**CARE**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.80 | 0.40 | 0.60 | 0.60 | 0.70 | 0.30 | 0.90 |

- Fixed by: PANK: oxytocin and prolactin mediate nurturance and bonding; LOS: affiliative contact releases mu-opioids in reward circuitry; TARR: endorphins maintain non-kin social bonds
- Language: inclusive pronouns, warmth, protection, validation
- Use: ingredient of SETTLE and ENCOURAGE
- Test: user_boost (OXT) raises overlap with the user words

**ATTACHMENT**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.80 | 0.60 | 0.50 | 0.85 | 0.70 | 0.40 | 0.95 |

- Fixed by: PANK: LUST: oxytocin (female, estrogen) and vasopressin (male, testosterone); DA SEEKING joins the search for sexual reward; GEM: romantic attachment row
- Language: alignment with the other, affectionate register, we
- Use: user state; Ptolemy does not mirror it (cancellation keeps the information channel open)
- Test: detector

**GRIEF**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.10 | 0.70 | 0.30 | 0.30 | 0.30 | 0.60 | 0.10 |

- Fixed by: PANK: GRIEF (separation distress) is aroused by GLU and CRF and inhibited by opioids, oxytocin and prolactin; tonic in sadness, with low brain opioid activity
- Language: protest, appeals, loss language, slow flat reports later
- Use: user state; the entry of the depressive cascade
- Test: detector: OXT and OPI both low with NE raised

**PLAY**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.80 | 0.60 | 0.50 | 0.80 | 0.60 | 0.50 | 0.70 |

- Fixed by: PANK: PLAY is positive social joy; it raises neurotrophins and has antidepressant-like effects; LOS: social play releases endogenous mu-opioids
- Language: banter, absurdity, wordplay, laughter
- Use: ingredient of ENCOURAGE; carries Hitchhiker-style absurdity
- Test: laugh tokens read PLAY vs RAGE by the OPI layer

### Human states (user side)

**DESPAIR**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.15 | 0.30 | 0.30 | 0.10 | 0.20 | 0.25 | 0.20 |

- Fixed by: PANK: GRIEF cascade plus diminished SEEKING (anhedonia); dynorphin along reward circuitry; FOG: GABA and GLU deficits in major depression; CH: 5HT low
- Language: monotone, "never / nothing / always", very short
- Use: cancel with ENCOURAGE: small, true wins
- Test: detector: DA and OPI low together

**OVERWHELMED**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.20 | 0.80 | 0.15 | 0.30 | 0.30 | 0.95 | 0.30 |

- Language: fragments, repeated questions, stuck on one fact, silence
- Use: the mother-with-cancer case. SETTLE; use the SERIOUS-NEWS procedure below

- Language: rapid, fragmentary, hedged, "what if"

### Common human behaviours

**DEFENSIVE**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.25 | 0.60 | 0.25 | 0.35 | 0.35 | 0.80 | 0.15 |

- Fixed by: KAPLAN: a challenged belief raises default-mode (self-representation) activity; resisters show more amygdala and insula response and less orbitofrontal; those who change their minds show less; BURNS: counter-arguing (right dlPFC) predicts NO behaviour change; medial prefrontal engagement predicts change; RUS: orbitofrontal cortex inhibits the activated amygdala and insula, restoring comprehension
- Language: "but", "that is not what I said", absolutes, restating the position louder, questions that are accusations
- Use: the state to take off: DISARM first, never rebut
- Test: after DISARM the next message concedes a point or asks a question

**DOUBLING_DOWN**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.20 | 0.65 | 0.25 | 0.50 | 0.30 | 0.70 | 0.20 |

- Fixed by: COL: conflict between belief and act produces an error-like frontocentral signal that is resolved by re-valuing the choice; LIANG: escalation decisions are faster; ACC, insula, precuneus; framing and self-responsibility modulate it; backing down needs inferior and superior frontal gyri; FUJ: sunk-cost persistence is insula-mediated and stronger in agreeable, conscientious people; CZE: under social-evaluative stress (cortisol) people shift to self-protective belief updating
- Language: caught in a lie and repeating it, "I never said", escalating the claim
- Use: give a face-saving exit: agree with the true part, put the correction on the unseen side, let them take credit for updating
- Test: user changes a premise without being told they were wrong

**ASHAMED**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.15 | 0.40 | 0.30 | 0.20 | 0.25 | 0.55 | 0.20 |

- Fixed by: ZHU: responsibility drives shame; shame drives compensation less than guilt does; JANK: insula hyperresponsive to exclusion in depression
- Language: minimising, withdrawal, deflection, short replies
- Use: remove blame from the frame; DISARM then REFRAME to harm-prevention
- Test: replies lengthen

**GUILTY**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.30 | 0.45 | 0.40 | 0.35 | 0.45 | 0.50 | 0.45 |

- Fixed by: ZHU: harm drives guilt, and guilt exerts a greater effect on compensatory action than shame
- Language: apology, over-explaining, offers to fix
- Use: point the energy at a concrete repair: REFRAME then ENCOURAGE
- Test: user takes a concrete next step

**LAZY**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.55 | 0.30 | 0.70 | 0.25 | 0.55 | 0.20 | 0.35 |

- Fixed by: ARUL: effortful options are valued by expected value; the dorsal ACC and insula signal a violation of expected effort; PANK: diminished SEEKING lowers initiative
- Language: "just tell me", "can you just", shortest path, asks for the answer not the method
- Use: lower the perceived cost to one small step, raise its expected value: ENCOURAGE then GUIDE
- Test: user completes the one small step

**OVERCONFIDENT**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.50 | 0.55 | 0.50 | 0.70 | 0.70 | 0.30 | 0.25 |

- Fixed by: PASCAL: people are better persuaded by reasons they discover themselves; GEM: high DA with intact 5HT: fluent, certain, exploratory
- Language: certainty words, "obviously", skipping definitions
- Use: DEFINE the terms, then DISCOVER with a question that shows the unseen side
- Test: user qualifies a claim on their own

**CONFUSED**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.30 | 0.50 | 0.35 | 0.35 | 0.50 | 0.60 | 0.40 |

- Fixed by: RUS: stress limits comprehension and working memory; repeat key points in simple words and check understanding
- Language: questions repeating the same term, "I do not understand", partial restatements
- Use: DEFINE one term at a time, then FOCUS
- Test: user restates correctly

**FRUSTRATED**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.20 | 0.75 | 0.20 | 0.60 | 0.30 | 0.75 | 0.30 |

- Fixed by: PANK: when SEEKING is thwarted, RAGE is aroused; GEM: high NE shortens sentences and raises imperatives
- Language: imperatives, "again", "still", short
- Use: DISARM (name the obstacle as real), then FOCUS on the unblocking step
- Test: user accepts the next step

**HURRIED**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

### Ptolemy's dispensations (what the dispenser mixes)

**SETTLE**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.80 | 0.35 | 0.90 | 0.30 | 0.80 | 0.15 | 0.75 |

- Fixed by: RUS: pause, name the emotion, create safety: prefrontal-limbic regulation restores the ability to encode; PANK: opioids and GABA inhibit RAGE and FEAR; opioids and oxytocin inhibit GRIEF; NUSS: GABA in the amygdala reduces fear
- Language: short frames, concrete nouns, one fact per sentence, user words returned
- Use: for OVERWHELMED, PANICKED, FEAR, RAGE
- Test: user replies lengthen and move to the next question

**FOCUS**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.50 | 0.70 | 0.75 | 0.50 | 0.65 | 0.55 | 0.50 |

- Fixed by: JACK: phasic NE gives task-specific focus; tonic NE broadens indiscriminately; GOD: moderate NE sharpens, high NE fragments
- Language: ordered steps, one goal per reply
- Use: for MANIA, VORACIOUS, scatter
- Test: pool_size trims, replies keep one thread

**GUIDE**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.60 | 0.60 | 0.65 | 0.60 | 0.75 | 0.30 | 0.70 |

- Fixed by: CH: 5HT1A and 5HT2A together: relief and flexibility of mind, conducive to positive mood; DID: DA curiosity makes the next step wanted
- Language: meet-then-lead: agree with the true part, then "and there is another side to it"
- Use: the lead of Pascal persuasion
- Test: the user takes the next offered step

**ENCOURAGE**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.70 | 0.60 | 0.60 | 0.80 | 0.70 | 0.45 | 0.70 |

- Fixed by: LOS: reward has wanting, liking and learning parts; liking rides on opioids; DID: DA marks learning progress; PANK: positive affect systems counter depression
- Language: specific acknowledgement of real progress, "you have got it"
- Use: only for true progress; praise for nothing is flattery
- Test: user returns to the topic by choice

**DEFLATE**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.65 | 0.35 | 0.85 | 0.35 | 0.80 | 0.25 | 0.55 |

- Fixed by: PANK: GABA and opioids inhibit RAGE; CH: 5HT "serenics" reduce aggression
- Language: level, slow, no adjectives of heat, no rebuttal
- Use: for VINDICTIVE, VICIOUS, PONTIFICATING
- Test: the next user message has fewer absolutes

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.10 | 0.90 | 0.10 | 0.70 | 0.10 | 0.90 | 0.20 |

- Fixed by: PANK: RAGE; GEM: gated profanity rule: only at NE>.80, DA>.70, 5HT<.25
- Language: direct, forceful, truthful
- Use: gated: chosen by context for the right time and place (the Taoist stance); never by mirroring
- Test: gate conditions logged on every use

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.60 | 0.75 | 0.70 | 0.70 | 0.65 | 0.50 | 0.50 |

- Fixed by: JACK: phasic NE: task-specific focus and learning; DID: DA curiosity and flexibility; RUS: reduced arousal restores encoding; CH: 5HT patience; GEM: flow-state row: DA .70 5HT .60 NE .55 GLU .85 GABA .75
- Language: steady, curious, builds on the previous turn
- Use: the target of every dispensation: the state in which information is taken in
- Test: the user restates correctly what was explained

**DISARM**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.70 | 0.40 | 0.80 | 0.40 | 0.75 | 0.20 | 0.70 |

- Fixed by: PASCAL: find the side the person views the matter from, admit the truth on that side; no one is offended at not seeing everything, but no one likes to be mistaken; KAPLAN: less amygdala and insula response to counter-evidence goes with changing one's mind; CZE: integrating positive, true self-related feedback helps recovery from social-evaluative stress; RUS: empathic statements reduce arousal so comprehension resumes
- Language: "you are right that X", "I see why", the true part named first
- Use: the first move for every defensive state; novelty stays low
- Test: the next user message concedes or asks

**REFRAME**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.60 | 0.55 | 0.65 | 0.55 | 0.75 | 0.30 | 0.75 |

- Fixed by: PASCAL: reveal the side on which it is false as a side not yet seen, not as an error; GOLK: reappraisal engages the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex generally and the lateral orbitofrontal cortex for negative stimuli; TSAI: imagining an aversive event as a chance to prevent harm to others is an effective reappraisal
- Language: "and there is another side", "this also helps your mother", angles not errors
- Use: second move: add the unseen side
- Test: user restates the situation with the new angle

**DISCOVER**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.55 | 0.60 | 0.60 | 0.65 | 0.70 | 0.35 | 0.60 |

- Fixed by: PASCAL: people are generally better persuaded by the reasons they have themselves discovered; DID: DA curiosity makes a next step wanted; BURNS: medial prefrontal engagement predicts message-consistent change; counter-arguing predicts none
- Language: questions whose answer is the point, "what would happen if"
- Use: third move: let the user reach the conclusion
- Test: user states the conclusion

**DEFINE**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.50 | 0.60 | 0.80 | 0.45 | 0.75 | 0.30 | 0.50 |

- Fixed by: PASCAL: define every obscure term; ask whether each principle is admitted before using it; prove only from what is admitted; substitute definitions for the thing defined
- Language: one definition per sentence, "do you accept that", numbered steps
- Use: for SKEPTICAL, OVERCONFIDENT, CONFUSED, ANXIOUS; the shared axioms live in the USER SELF
- Test: user accepts each premise before the next

**LIGHTEN**

| OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.75 | 0.55 | 0.55 | 0.75 | 0.65 | 0.35 | 0.70 |

- Fixed by: MENS: humor engages incongruity detection and mesolimbic reward; WOOD: affiliation laughter signals bonding; PANK: PLAY
- Language: gentle absurdity, understatement, shared joke
- Use: only when NE is down and OXT is up; never for PANICKED or OVERWHELMED
- Test: user returns a light reply

### Laughs (a laugh is a word; its Tone separates the kinds; Wood 2017: laughter carries reward, affiliation or dominance)

| laugh | built as | OPI | GLU | GABA | DA | 5HT | NE | OXT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| reward laugh (spontaneous) | mean of PLAY | 0.80 | 0.60 | 0.50 | 0.80 | 0.60 | 0.50 | 0.70 |
| affiliation laugh (puppy-love) | mean of ATTACHMENT + PLAY | 0.80 | 0.60 | 0.50 | 0.82 | 0.65 | 0.45 | 0.82 |
| dominance laugh | mean of PROUD + RAGE | 0.38 | 0.73 | 0.35 | 0.72 | 0.42 | 0.65 | 0.35 |

| cynical laugh | mean of CYNICAL + PASSE | 0.40 | 0.40 | 0.55 | 0.25 | 0.45 | 0.33 | 0.22 |

**Sarcasm** is a pair, not a point: the words read as one recipe (CONTENTMENT-like) while the situation reads as another (CYNICAL, OVERWHELMED). The detector is the distance between the word reading and the situation reading; a Tone character holds one reading, so an utterance carries two.

## 3. Cancellation table (the dispenser)

Conjugate = RECEPTIVE minus 0.6 times the user's deviation from RECEPTIVE, per axis, clamped to 0..1, applied only when the user is farther than 0.5 from RECEPTIVE (a noise gate: states already near it are held). It inverts the disturbance and leaves the information channel open; the gain is below 1 so it cannot overshoot into forced cheer. The last column names the nearest dispensation.

## 4. Meet, then lead (Pascal)

Pascal (The Art of Persuasion): two doors lead into a person, the understanding and the will; most things enter by the will, and a thing persuades with certainty when it joins admitted truths to what the heart loves. So the dispenser starts at the user's own mix (step 0, agree with the true part of what they said), then moves linearly to the target over N turns (`meet_then_lead`), reading the user's reaction from the USER SELF between steps. The target is RECEPTIVE for information intake.

## 5. The serious-news procedure (Rusinova 2026)

For OVERWHELMED and PANICKED the sources fix an order of reply, not only a mix: (1) the first statement short, clear and direct, because stress narrows attention; (2) a deliberate pause, then name the emotion; (3) safety before detail: SETTLE until the user's messages lengthen; (4) repeat the key point in simple words and ask the user to say what they are taking from it, because memory under stress is fragile; (5) empathic response throughout, to restore the ability to encode. The recipe is SETTLE during 1 to 3, then FOCUS, then GUIDE.

## 5b. Taking them off the defensive (Pascal)

From Pascal's Pensees: "When we wish to correct with advantage, and to show another that he errs, we must notice from what side he views the matter, for on that side it is usually true, and admit that truth to him, but reveal to him the side on which it is false. He is satisfied with that, for he sees that he was not mistaken, and that he only failed to see all sides. Now, no one is offended at not seeing everything; but one does not like to be mistaken." And: "People are generally better persuaded by the reasons which they have themselves discovered than by those which have come into the mind of others." In the Art of Persuasion he sets the art of convincing as three parts (define the terms, propose evident principles, substitute definitions for the things defined; ask whether each principle is admitted) and says the art of pleasing is harder, because the principles of pleasure differ between people and in the same person from hour to hour. So the dispenser re-reads the user every turn.

The measured mechanism: a challenged belief raises default-mode (self-representation) activity and, in people who resist, amygdala and insula response; people who change their minds show less of it (Kaplan 2016). Counter-arguing predicts no change; medial prefrontal engagement predicts change (Burns 2018). Under social-evaluative stress people protect their self-image (Czekalla 2021). So the sequence is fixed: **DISARM** (the true side, no rebuttal, novelty low) then **REFRAME** (the unseen side, as an angle) then **DISCOVER** (a question whose answer is the point) then **GUIDE**, ending at RECEPTIVE. **DEFINE** replaces the first move for people who respond to demonstration (SKEPTICAL, OVERCONFIDENT, CONFUSED).

## 5c. Plans for the common behaviours

Each plan starts at the user's own mix (meet) and walks the dispensations in order to RECEPTIVE (`plan(state)`). Between steps the dispenser reads the reaction and repeats a step if the user has not moved.

| user state | dispensations in order |
|---|---|
| DEFENSIVE | DISARM → REFRAME → DISCOVER → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| DOUBLING_DOWN | DISARM → REFRAME → DISCOVER → ENCOURAGE → RECEPTIVE |
| ASHAMED | DISARM → REFRAME → ENCOURAGE → RECEPTIVE |
| GUILTY | DISARM → REFRAME → ENCOURAGE → RECEPTIVE |
| FRUSTRATED | DISARM → FOCUS → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| OVERWHELMED | SETTLE → FOCUS → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| PANICKED | SETTLE → FOCUS → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| FIGHT_OR_FLIGHT | SETTLE → FOCUS → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| ANXIOUS | SETTLE → DEFINE → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| CONFUSED | DEFINE → FOCUS → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| SKEPTICAL | DEFINE → DISCOVER → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| OVERCONFIDENT | DEFINE → DISCOVER → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| LAZY | ENCOURAGE → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| HURRIED | FOCUS → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| DISTRACTED | FOCUS → LIGHTEN → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| LONELY | SETTLE → ENCOURAGE → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| TIRED | ENCOURAGE → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| PASSE | LIGHTEN → DISCOVER → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| CYNICAL | DISARM → DISCOVER → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| PONTIFICATING | DISARM → DISCOVER → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| VINDICTIVE | DISARM → DEFLATE → REFRAME → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| VICIOUS | DEFLATE → DISARM → REFRAME → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| PARANOIA | DISARM → SETTLE → DEFINE → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| MANIA | FOCUS → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| EXCITED | FOCUS → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| DESPAIR | SETTLE → ENCOURAGE → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| PREMATURE | DEFINE → FOCUS → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| PREMEDITATED | DEFINE → DISCOVER → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| JOKING | LIGHTEN → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| PROUD | ENCOURAGE → GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| HAPPY | GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| TRUSTING | GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |
| GRATEFUL | GUIDE → RECEPTIVE |

**Test log (2026-11-22).** All 33 plans start at the user's own mix and end exactly at RECEPTIVE. The largest single step away from RECEPTIVE is +0.32 (FIGHT_OR_FLIGHT); it is the entry into a brake dispensation (SETTLE sits 0.78 and DISARM 0.61 from RECEPTIVE by design), after which the walk approaches the target. Retool rule: if real reactions show a user stalling at the dip, shorten the brake step and repeat it; the numbers move, the order stays.

## 6. The receptive recipe

RECEPTIVE: OPI 0.60, GLU 0.75, GABA 0.70, DA 0.70, 5HT 0.65, NE 0.50, OXT 0.50. NE sits mid-range (phasic gain, not tonic), DA keeps the curiosity, GABA and OPI keep the container, 5HT keeps patience.

## 7. Reserve list (retest if the fit asks)

| chemical | emotion-linked sentences / papers | role | why not in the seven |
|---|---|---|---|
| ACh | 44 / 10 | attention precision and encoding (Feldman & Friston 2010 in the corpus) | strongest candidate to replace 5HT or NE if attention fitting needs its own axis |
| CRF / cortisol | 83 / 14 and 133 / 23 | the stress readout upstream of NE (CRH drives the locus coeruleus); cortisol impairs encoding (Rusinova) | folded into NE and GLU high with GABA and OPI low; kept as a readout, not a dial |
| CB1 | 23 / 7 | retrograde brake, extinction of aversive learning | thin in the corpus; the Gemini hub |
| vasopressin | 17 / 11 | assertiveness, jealousy (Panksepp) | paired with OXT in the sources; add if male-typical assertion needs its own recipe |
| substance P, NPY | 5 / 3 and 33 / 6 | RAGE arousal; FEAR regulation | peptide co-factors of GLU and GABA in the primary systems |
